headline: Modular, reusable representations of phage, mobile element and accessory gene content in microbial genomes
label: Microbial Mobilome And Pangenome Resources
summary: New phage fragment annotations, a 16.4M-element MGE database, a prophage workflow and S. aureus NMF modules expand structured views of microbial genome content.
synthesis: The dominant thread is decomposing microbial genome content into reusable modular units, with emphasis on mobile and accessory elements. Conserved-fragment HMM comparisons across 5,396 phage genomes yield 13,035 fragments annotating 50% of phage proteins, extending beyond Pfam and ECOD. proMGE2 catalogues over 16.4 million mobile genetic elements from isolates and MAGs, with a 5-million-sequence non-redundant set. PHI packages prophage identification, quality assessment, host prediction and functional annotation in a Galaxy workflow with standardized reporting. In S. aureus, non-negative matrix factorization of 1,398 genomes splits the accessory pangenome into 24 additive gene modules separating lineage from adaptation and virulence. Scales and organisms differ, but each item offers structured, reusable representations of variable gene content.
